title: Personal portfolio
learningObjectives: Complete personal portfolio using the project's existing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and engineering practices.

understand.concept: A portfolio presents a person's work, skills, background, and contact route. It should prioritise clear navigation, project evidence, accessible content, responsive layout, and privacy-aware contact information. Claims should be accurate and project links should work.
understand.whyItMatters: A portfolio helps visitors evaluate work quickly. Real examples and clear explanations are more useful than decorative effects or unsupported claims.
understand.analogy: A portfolio is an organised exhibition where each project has a clear label and explanation.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; project requirements and release quality must be verified against the actual implementation and user needs.

explain.narrative: The starter provides a semantic portfolio structure. Learners should replace sample content with their own accurate project descriptions.

practise.guidedTask: Build a multi-section portfolio with introduction, skills, project cards, and contact method. Test keyboard access and mobile layout.
practise.independentTask: Complete the task in a project repository. Keep the scope explicit, preserve user privacy, test the main workflow, and document evidence and known limitations.
hints: Plan before coding and keep changes focused.
Use semantic HTML and reusable responsive CSS.
Test keyboard access, edge cases, and deployment behaviour.
